title: DADS5250 Section Recording Script
recording_plan: Record the nine sections separately in Sound Recorder using your own voice. Keep a short quiet lead and tail on each clip. Do not read the headings, bold-format explanation or Japanese screen cues.
style: Short sentences. Main verbs are marked separately for a bold reading copy. Each sentence is on its own line. Use a natural short pause after each sentence.
editing_note: Final timing must use the actual supplied audio. Keep natural pauses and screen interaction time. Do not force an eight-to-ten-minute result by unnatural voice speed changes or fabricate approval footage.

sections.title: The problem and the project
sections.screen_cue_ja: 氏名とSoloを表示し、業務フロー図からアプリへ切り替える。

lines.text: Hello, I am Satoshi Nakamura.
This is my solo final project for DADS five two five zero.
I built an AI assistant for data engineering requests.
Business users often prefer a spreadsheet.
They ask for a report, a data extract, or a BI change.
A business analyst checks the need, value, and timing.
BA means business analyst.
A data engineer then plans and tests the change.
My app supports this flow, with two human decisions.
The demo ends with a reviewed patch package.
It does not merge code or release a production change.

sections.title: The request sheet
sections.screen_cue_ja: 合成データのGoogle Sheetを見せた後、Google Sheetsを選びRefresh Google Sheetsを押す。

lines.text: This is our private demo sheet.
All requests use made-up business data.
Users write the need and the expected result.
The BA adds notes about impact, priority, and dates.
These fields keep the discussion together.
A new row does not start development on its own.
I select Google Sheets and click Refresh in the app.
The app reads the private sheet through my Google login.
This path needs no CSV download or upload.
The app has read-only access.
It does not change the sheet or its sharing settings.
The screen shows the rows and refresh time.

sections.title: Impact and change size
sections.screen_cue_ja: OpenAI APIを選択し、対象リストと推定結果のマトリクスを映す。数値は実際の画面に合わせる。

lines.text: I select OpenAI API mode for real AI estimates.
The other mode uses fixed sample rules.
The screen labels each mode.
I choose the review list and ask for estimates.
The app compares business impact with change size.
Impact comes from the request and the BA notes.
Change size comes from the sample project files.
A high-impact, small change can come first.
A larger change may need smaller phases.
Missing facts stay visible as unknowns.
The app compares fixed templates with current project files.
For a supported revenue rule, the app counts files and changed lines.
These counts give a rough scope.
They do not show exact working hours.
The BA still checks readiness, priority, and timing.
The AI suggests a choice.
A person makes the decision.

sections.title: The first human decision
sections.screen_cue_ja: REQ-001の要件と根拠を読み、本人がBAの理由と確認を入力する。Goの成立は実際の画面で確認する。

lines.text: I choose the campaign revenue request.
The agreed rule excludes canceled orders from revenue.
Here, revenue means the sum of order amounts.
The BA notes explain why the change matters.
I check those notes and the project evidence.
Then I enter a reason for the BA decision.
The BA can choose Go, Hold, or Clarify.
The app checks the latest source again before Go.
It rejects a review if the source has changed.
A valid Go saves the agreed request as a fixed ticket.
The ticket follows a Jira-style flow.
The app does not create a real Jira issue.

sections.title: The three course techniques
sections.screen_cue_ja: Prepare and validate、Ticket JSON、根拠ファイル、変更計画を見せる。待ち時間にはアーキテクチャ図を使える。

lines.text: Next, I prepare and check the change.
The app combines three course techniques.
The first technique is Structured Output.
The model creates a ticket with a fixed format.
The app checks that format and the business rule.
The app pauses when the rule is unclear.
The second technique is RAG.
RAG means retrieval augmented generation.
The app searches approved project files for useful text.
It uses word matches and known revenue links.
The screen shows the source file paths.
I can compare the plan with that evidence.
The third technique is an agent workflow with LangGraph.
LangGraph controls the ticket, plan, and check stages.
The app treats request text as untrusted data.
The model proposes changes within a small, fixed scope.
The app allows changes to four files only.
A request cannot add a new file or a new command.
The model cannot run its own commands.

sections.title: The changes and real checks
sections.screen_cue_ja: 実際の6検証、差分、元の合計と期待値を見せる。920と770の行はREQ-001が実際に通った場合のみ使用する。
sections.requires_matching_video: Use the primary numbered-result lines only when REQ-001 actually shows original 920 and expected/proposed 770 with passing checks. Otherwise record the alternative section after reviewing the real outcome.

lines.text: The screen shows the changes and test results.
The original total is nine hundred twenty in this checked example.
The expected total is seven hundred seventy.
The proposed total is also seven hundred seventy.
The app runs real checks, not an AI opinion about the code.
It checks file scope and the separate work folder.
It loads trusted sample data and runs dbt tests.
An independent check calculates the expected revenue.
Python tests compare the daily results with the sample orders.
The four files contain SQL, a test, project notes, and dashboard rules.
The dashboard rules stay in a text file.
They do not update Looker Studio.
A failed check blocks approval.

alternative_if_failed: The review screen shows a failed check.
The app blocks approval for this result.
I need to review the issue and request a revision.
I will not treat this result as an approved change.
The report also includes one earlier live example with six passing checks.
That example is separate from the result on this screen.

sections.title: The second human decision
sections.screen_cue_ja: 本人がHuman reviewで内容を確認し、承認または修正を判断する。Downloadの画面は実際の承認後にだけ見せる。

lines.text: The second human decision reviews the proposed change.
The first decision allowed work to start.
This decision checks the result of that work.
I review the evidence, the file changes, and the tests.
I approve only when the result meets the agreed rule.
Otherwise, I ask for a revision.
The app offers a patch package after approval.
The package includes files, test results, and the decision record.
The app checks that the package matches the reviewed result.
It does not merge code or release the change.
The reviewer types a name into this local demo.
That name does not prove that two people reviewed it.

sections.title: A request that needs more work
sections.screen_cue_ja: BA intakeに戻り、未準備のREQ-009を見せる。実際のHoldまたはClarifyと不足情報を示す。

lines.text: Now I show a request that is not ready.
This mobile-push request has an urgent date.
But the BA still needs example events and an agreed time rule.
An urgent date does not fill those gaps.
The app keeps the missing facts visible.
The BA can choose Hold or Clarify.
A high rank does not make the request ready.
A new dashboard or data source also needs more scope work.
This demo only prepares changes to the existing revenue rule.
The safety checks also have limits.
They block known unsafe patterns.
They may miss new attacks.

sections.title: Results and next steps
sections.screen_cue_ja: レポートの結果表、READMEのセットアップ、GitHubを見せる。過去の個別検証と今回の録画を区別する。

lines.text: The results cover different kinds of tests.
The automated suite passed one hundred and three tests.
The fixed sample tests covered six normal requests.
They blocked three attack examples and paused one unclear request.
These sample results do not measure general AI accuracy.
One separate live OpenAI check passed all six delivery checks.
It covered one request and stopped before human approval.
A separate Google check read ten request rows.
Those connection checks were separate tests.
The source code includes setup steps, sample data, and tests.
It includes no API keys or Google tokens.
Future work includes more data models, stronger user roles, and Jira.
The goal is a useful change that people can check.
Thank you for watching.

pronunciation_guide.meaning_ja: この台本では1文字ずつでよい。
コース番号は数字を1つずつ読む。
太い大文字の音節を少し強く読む目安。
RAGの正式名称で1度だけ使う。
retrievalの後でひと呼吸してもよい。
売上。数字の前後をゆっくり読む。
入力を、そのまま指示として信用しないという意味。

do_not_need_to_say: The exact configured model ID can appear on screen instead of being read aloud.
The local retrieval implementation is TF-IDF cosine ranking with fixed revenue dependency expansion. The spoken version describes it as word matches and known revenue links.
The dashboard artifact is a custom YAML definition. The spoken version calls it dashboard rules in a text file.
accuracy_notes: Private Google input and live OpenAI generation must be visible in their actual modes. Any sample fallback needs its own spoken label.
Section 06 numbered results require matching actual passing REQ-001 footage; otherwise use a revised failure clip.
Section 07 states an approval rule and the behavior after approval; the video must show the presenter making the real decision before showing an export.
The prior live OpenAI and Google checks were separate. No combined earlier human-approved run is claimed.
reading_notes_ja: 1行を1つの文として読む。太字は主な動詞または動詞句。強く読み上げる指示ではない。録音時間は実音声で確認する。
